correctness.rationale: Rook distance is Hamming distance, so the only forbidden triples are 144 three-corner L shapes (72 nonadjacent pairs, two middle vertices each). Independently recognized the same rule by requiring every selected square to be alone in at least one of its selected row or column: a violation supplies an L, and conversely. Enumerated the f-vector (16,120,416,632,240,16), so the maximum facet dimension is five. Reconstructed the 670 disjoint pairs on the nonempty face poset and topologically sorted all 5312 oriented covers. The critical cells are one vertex, 98 three-cells and one four-cell; discrete Morse theory gives a homotopy-equivalent CW model, not a claim of elementary simplicial collapse to an abstract wedge. Independently reduced the signed boundary of the critical 4-cell in DAG order using 191 nonzero unit-pivot updates. Each update subtracts the boundary of the matching upper cell, with its orientation determined by the position of the deleted vertex. The zero residual in the full 3-chain group leaves zero Morse boundary; neither torsion nor nullhomotopy is inferred from finite-field Betti numbers. Below the sole 4-cell the CW model is a wedge of 98 three-spheres; Hurewicz identifies π₃ with H₃ there, so zero integral attaching degrees prove nullhomotopy and the claimed wedge.
residual_risks: This is only the four-by-four board; no equivariant or all-rectangles claim.

evidence: The three-row theorem gives GP(K₃□K_n) ≃ (∨^(2^n)S^(n−1)) ∨ (∨^n S²) for n≥3; swapping factors still cannot produce K₄□K₄.

The product-independence article computes independence complexes for path-containing products, not the whole GP complex of a complete-graph product. Iršič et al. and Rather study counting polynomials and their coefficients.
broader_coverage.reasoning: There is no applicable more general homotopy theorem in these inspected results. A known 12-vertex K₃□K₄ case is a different complex even though some of its reduced homology is in degree three.

value.rationale: Determines the complete wedge type and the two nonzero reduced integral homology groups of a natural board complex, despite maximal simplices in dimension five. This is genuinely different data from face enumeration: identifying the wedge requires verifying a null attachment. The balanced board is a useful exact reference for the broader problem of topologizing graph general-position sets or bipartite star forests.
